summary: Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Latymer Upper School and the University of Cambridge (Emmanuel College) from circa 1969 to 1972, under Nai Boonman, and under Ajahn Chah in 1974. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery circa 1983.
Ajahn Khemadhammo works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Drama Centre London from circa 1963 to 1966 and trained under his traditional teacher Ajahn Chah from circa 1972 to 1977.
Ajahn Pasanno works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ajahn Chah from circa 1974 to 1982 and served as founding co-abbot at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from circa 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied English and American literature at the University of Warwick (circa 1968–1971) and under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho works in Buddhist studies. He earned master's degrees from the University of Washington and UC Berkeley, and studied under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He founded and was abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and served as abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in the field of Indology. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao (1979–2002). His appointments include Ryukoku University, Shinshu Otaniha Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held faculty and administrative posts at Kyushu University, Kyoto University, and the Hakubi Center for Advanced Research.

Akihiro Oda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University. He served on the faculty at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 1992 and as Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2013.
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).

Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (circa 1994–2001) and Harvard University (circa 2001–2009), and held an academic post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.

Akio Donohashi is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1968 to 1978 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an associate professor at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), conducted overseas research at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is attested as faculty at the Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Akio Tanabe works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his degrees from the University of Tokyo, where he became a professor in 2015. He also held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993) and Kyoto University (1998, 2004).
Akio Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who spent his career at Ryukoku University, where he is attested as an assistant professor in 1987 and as professor emeritus in 2015.

Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1931–1934), where he later served as professor (1968), and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).

Akira Hataya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there (1962–1975). He also taught at Waseda University and served as president of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

Akira Miyaji specialized in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University, he served on its faculty until becoming professor emeritus, and held posts at Hirosaki University, Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University and Museum.
